finding.claim: Blind SSRF: subscribe() stores an unvalidated callbackUrl and notifyAll() POSTs to it every minute from the server's network position, with no scheme, host, resolved-IP or DNS-pinning check.
finding.source: callbackUrl parameter of subscribe() at src/Jobs.java:13 (per comment at line 12, from POST /subscribe body; handler not in repo, assumed reachable by untrusted users)
finding.sink: client.send(req, ...) at src/Jobs.java:24, POST to URI.create(cb) at src/Jobs.java:21

trace.note: subscriptions.put(name, callbackUrl) stores it unchanged, no validation
notifyAll iterates over all stored callback values
POST body is server-chosen payload passed in by caller
client.send issues the request; response body discarded so blind

finding.guards_checked: subscribe-time: none (raw store). send-time: none (no scheme allowlist, host allowlist, private/loopback/link-local/metadata IP check, or DNS pinning). Redirects: not followed, HttpClient.newHttpClient() defaults to Redirect.NEVER (src/Jobs.java:10). Schemes: java.net.http accepts only http/https, so file:/gopher: are rejected at request build; internal http(s) hosts remain reachable. Impact: blind, POST-only, fixed payload, repeats every minute; exceptions from URI.create/client.send abort the loop, giving a weak error-based oracle.

verdict.reason: The trace is accurate: src/Jobs.java:14 stores callbackUrl unchanged, :21 calls URI.create(cb) with no validation, and :24 sends the request, with no closing guard anywhere in the file (the only validation, the regex at :30, sits in thumb() and is not on this path). The source is unverifiable because the /subscribe handler that supplies callbackUrl is not in the repo (the only mention is the comment at src/Jobs.java:12), so I cannot tell whether an unauthenticated or low-privilege user can reach subscribe().
